_meta.description: REAL utility seed for UoF Business Plan Studio (Option A). Tagbilaran City Waterworks System (TCWS), Bohol, Philippines. Values transcribed from the 7 source documents listed in sources; gaps are null with gap_note. Prepared 2026-10-14.
transcription_checks: Monthly billed volume 2020-2025 equals printed annual totals (05)
Monthly production 2024 and Jan-Jun 2025 equal printed totals; 2023 monthly sum is 9 m3 below printed 3,535,036 (07)
Accounts by barangay sum to printed totals 2020-2025 (05)
open_issues: Financial model (02) divides required revenue by PWSP+BBWSP volume; PWSP equals private WSP supply in the demand analysis. Required tariff on TCWS volume only is about PhP 50/m3 (2030) vs 21.94.
Connections 2025: 6,314 (05, latest record) vs 6,084 (01, June 2025, older class breakdown).
OPEX 2022-2023 are calculated in 01 Table 16; OPEX 2024 is estimated from the should-be tariff.
Collections are used as water sales; billings are not available, so collection efficiency cannot be computed.
Draft JMC lists operating ratio 'at least 1.00'; the model's FORMULA sheet defines operating ratio = OPEX/revenue, so the target is applied as 1.00 or below.

service.water_quality: Distribution side good, no customer complaints; 10% failure in sampling (SWOT)

narratives.Commercial: Connections grew from 5,612 (2020) to 6,461 (2024); billed volume stayed between 1.70 and 1.90 million m3 per year. Collections rose from PhP 18.7 M to 23.1 M (2023) and dipped in 2024. The tariff is unchanged since 2016, so revenue per billed m3 is about PhP 12.
narratives.Technical: All water comes from 28 deep-well pumping stations with chlorination. NRW fell from about 46% (2023) to 31% (H1 2025), partly because production fell from 3.5 to 3.0 million m3. Supply is 22-24 hours a day.
narratives.Financial: OPEX rose from PhP 17.1 M (2020) to 26.1 M (2023, calculated), above collections from 2023 (operating ratio 1.13). The should-be tariff to recover OPEX was PhP 17.68/m3 in 2024.
narratives.Human talent: 24 staff (9 regular, 15 job order); multi-tasking and training needs flagged in the SWOT.
narratives._note: Draft narratives written from the source data; TCWS team to validate.

A2.1.vision_old: To manage our organization and water resources to meet evolving regulatory requirements, water supply needs, and customer expectations in the future.
A2.1.mission_old: Our mission is to provide our customers with safe and reliable water in compliance with regulatory requirements. We strive to treat every customer fairly and respectfully, and to address their needs quickly and effectively.
A2.1.vision: We want to become a world-class, sustainable waterworks by 2035. We want to achieve highly potable, 24/7 water supply. We see a more effective waterworks company capable of providing reliable and safe/clean water to every household in Tagbilaran City.
A2.1.mission: Our mission is to provide our customers in 10/15 barangays in Tagbilaran City with safe and reliable water. Our employees are capable and highly trained. We strive to treat every customer fairly and respectfully and address their needs quickly and effectively.

objectives.title: Improve billed volume
objectives.specific: Increase billed volume by expanding to unserved barangays, upgrading pumping stations and replacing inaccurate meters.
objectives.measurable: Billed volume (m3/yr) and connections; baseline 1,833,134 m3 (2024), 6,314 connections (2025).
objectives.relevant: Low coverage (33% of service area) and lack of water supply are key weaknesses.

objectives.title: Reduce NRW to 20%
objectives.specific: Reduce physical and commercial losses through DMAs, pipe replacement and detection of illegal connections.
objectives.relevant: NRW above the draft JMC standard (20% or below).
objectives.time_bound: Proposed path from demand analysis: 26% by 2030, 20% by 2035 (to be confirmed).

objectives.title: Improve collection efficiency
objectives.specific: Improve collection through disconnection enforcement and staggered AR payments.
objectives.measurable: Collection efficiency (%) = collections/billings; target at least 95% (draft JMC). Baseline not available.
objectives.relevant: Negative bottom line; tariff revenue is the only source.

objectives.title: Manage cost recovery
objectives.specific: Recover costs through ring-fenced LEE accounts and OPEX efficiency.
objectives.measurable: Operating ratio = OPEX/operating revenue; baseline 1.13 (2023); target 1.00 or below.
objectives.relevant: Tariff unchanged since 2016; should-be tariff 17.68 PhP/m3 (2024) vs about 12.5 collected per m3.

objectives.title: Manage / improve after-sales service
objectives.specific: Formalize customer service standards for complaints, leaks, illegal tapping, bulletins and new applications.
objectives.measurable: Share of cases resolved within the standard time.
objectives.relevant: Mayor: tariff increases must be balanced with better service.
